intent: Hold the iteration-6 geometry unchanged (five sensors at y = 0.07 m, x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.14 by 0.16 m body, 0.6 kg) so the Integrator's controller change is the only variable. Expect oval and s-bend to hold at 20 of 20, and slalom to stay limited by reversal reaction unless the controller changes that. Considered but not committed: (a) if slalom still fails at max_error near 0.063 m with progress near 0.26 to 0.30 and line losses near 1 per run, test wheel_track of about 0.10 m next iteration to see whether a narrower track speeds the reversal; (b) widen the spread to x = +/-0.032 m only if slalom line losses rise above about 2 per run with progress below 0.2; (c) revert to y = 0.06 m only if oval or s-bend completion drops below 20 of 20 and 18 of 20.
learning: Iterations 5 and 6 show that y = 0.07 m reduced oval and s-bend max_error without changing the slalom limit, so look-ahead is saturated. Hypothesis for this race: with geometry held, slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run, which points to a reversal-reaction limit that a controller change alone may not clear. If the slalom completes, the controller was the lever and geometry should stay put. If the slalom still fails with the same error signature, the next geometry test is wheel_track near 0.10 m, as planned by the Integrator.
rationale: Iteration 6 is the best race so far at 670.5. The oval finishes 20 of 20 and the s-bend finishes 20 of 20, up from 18 of 20 at iteration 5. The slalom still finishes 0 of 20, with progress 0.30, max_error 0.063 m (just over the 0.06 m limit) and 1.05 line-loss events per run. Line losses are far below the 2-per-run widening trigger, so the sensing spread is not the limit. The y = 0.07 m look-ahead has been tested: it helped the oval and s-bend error metrics and gave no slalom gain. The Integrator's feedback says the remaining slalom limit looks like reaction on the reversal, not sensing or look-ahead. Their next geometry step, wheel_track near 0.10 m, is only meant to be tested after the controller change is separated out. This iteration is that controller test, so the Integrator needs the geometry held unchanged. I am following that advice and holding the geometry exactly as in iterations 5 and 6. Changing wheel_track now would confound the controller result. The trigger for widening the spread (slalom line losses above about 2 per run with progress below 0.2) has not fired, and the body and mass are not constraints. I expect the geometry to behave as in iteration 6, and I am not stating a score outcome for the controller change itself.
